source: Rast, L. 2008. 'Husbandry and Reproduction', Best Practice Health & Husbandry of Cattle, Cambodia, workshop slides (mekonglivestock.wordpress.com)
text: The source lists practical benefits of using controlled (rather than free-roaming, unmanaged) mating: farmers know the pregnancy stage and expected birth date, can observe the birth itself (reducing injury/death risk to cow and calf), can plan calving for when it's needed most (e.g. for sale timing, or when labour and feed are easiest to manage), and can then provide the correct nutrition at each stage -- since a growing calf needs about 1.5 times maintenance energy and milk production for the calf needs about 2.5 times maintenance energy.
